raw_response:
I am 53 this year. I have farmed these 15 mu in Quzhou for 30 years, since I married into this village. I only finished primary school. My household has three people — my husband does some off-farm work in Handan city, and my son works in Beijing and sends money home. But this land is what we live on.

I have 10 mu that I plant wheat in autumn and maize in summer. The other 5 mu I grow cotton. That is what I have always done.

For wheat: Last October I sowed an improved variety, about 35 jin per mu. Before sowing I hired the tractor for rotary tillage and put down one 50-kilogram bag of compound fertilizer per mu. Now it is spring and the wheat is greening up. I will top-dress with one 50-kilogram bag of urea per mu — half at jointing and half at heading. I irrigate three times with my well: jointing water, heading water, and grain-filling water. I spray pesticide twice. I expect about 550 jin per mu. Three years ago I cut back to half a bag of urea to save money and lost almost 100 jin per mu. Never again. Fertilizer is 90 to 100 yuan a bag, but losing yield is a disaster.

For summer maize: After wheat harvest in early June, I plant hybrid maize seed, about 5 jin per mu. I do not till again — direct seeding into the wheat stubble. At sowing I put one bag of compound fertilizer per mu. When the plants are knee-high I top-dress with three-quarters of a bag of urea. I irrigate twice if the rain is not enough. Two pesticide sprays. I expect 600 jin per mu, maybe 650 if the weather is good.

For cotton on the 5 mu: In spring I plough the field deep, then sow hybrid cotton seed about 2.5 jin per mu. Cotton needs more care. I put one bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, then top-dress with urea and extra potassium fertilizer when it flowers. I irrigate twice and spray pesticide four times because bollworms love cotton. I expect around 320 jin of seed cotton per mu.

I decide this way because this is what I did last year and it worked. I watch my neighbors. If Lao Zhang and the others use one bag per mu, I use one bag per mu. I do not try new things unless I see them work on someone else's field first. I know fertilizer costs are high, but I would rather spend the money than risk a bad harvest. A bad harvest means I lose everything; wasting a little fertilizer is just a cost I can bear.
